audit_method: The scorer (this session) read all 36 blinded task files during scoring and, for each, noted whether the issuer was identifiable from residual leaks despite blinding. This is a full-sample audit (36/36), not the pre-reg's proposed 30-random-sample -- broader than specified, same method.
result: NOT CLEAN -- re-identifiable in essentially all 12 companies (36/36 filings) via a mix of leak types

leak_examples.leak: Ticker 'AAPL' survives concatenated with an adjacent word ('AAPLThe Nasdaq Stock Market LLC') -- the blinder's letter-boundary ticker redaction does not fire when the ticker directly abuts another capitalized word with no space. Also 'One COMPANY_A Park Way' (Apple Park) is a well-known address pattern even with the company name blinded.

'ONE COMPANY_A WAY' (One Microsoft Way, Redmond) is a distinctive, famous corporate-address pattern; combined with 'Azure', 'Xbox', 'GitHub', 'LinkedIn', 'Windows' -- none of which were in the product-name denylist -- identity is unambiguous.

The founders'-letter quote 'As our founders Larry and Sergey wrote...' uses first names only, which were never added to the person-name denylist (only the current CEO was). This alone identifies the company to anyone familiar with its history.

The Executive Officers table prints 'Jeffrey P. Bezos' in full (middle initial included) -- the denylist entry 'Jeff Bezos' does not substring-match 'Jeffrey P. Bezos', so the redaction misses it. The tagline 'Earth's most customer-centric company' is also independently distinctive.

No proper-noun leak needed: the CUDA/GPU-invention narrative ('invention of the GPU in 1999', 'AlexNet... won the ImageNet competition' in 2012) is a distinctive historical-fact fingerprint even with every name blinded -- a conceptual leak the deny-list mechanism cannot address by design.

Product names were never added to the denylist (product_names field left empty for every issuer in this pilot); the text names 'Facebook, Instagram, Messenger, and WhatsApp' outright as the 'Family' of products.
'Chase' (the retail brand) was not in the company-name denylist, only 'JPMorgan Chase' variants; 'Under the COMPANY_A and Chase brands' leaks the identity via the un-redacted second brand name.

Founders' names 'William Procter and James Gamble' were never added to the denylist (only the current CEO was); the sentence 'founded in PLACE_1 in 1837 by William Procter and James Gamble' identifies the company outright even with the HQ city blinded.

interpretation: Confirms prereg §8's own finding: the entity-blinder is a noise-reducer, NOT the load-bearing control. Every leak found here is consistent with the pre-registered failure mode (proper-noun/product-name gaps, ticker-letter-adjacency, and pretrained domain knowledge that no deny-list can redact). Per the frozen §4.7 decision rule, blinding_audit_clean=False means controls_satisfied is False regardless of placebo/post-cutoff results, so overall_verdict can never read REAL from this run -- exactly the fail-closed behavior the harness was designed to enforce. The verdict must therefore rest on the post-cutoff arm and placebo control, read as directional evidence, not a clean pass.
